overview.title: International Monetary Fund
overview.definition: An international organization of 190 member countries working to foster global monetary cooperation, secure financial stability, facilitate international trade, promote high employment and sustainable economic growth, and reduce poverty around the world.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Crucial for UPSC CSE Prelims (factual questions on SDRs, voting rights, quotas, and reports) and Mains GS Paper II & III (global economic governance, multilateral institutions, balance of payment crises, and structural adjustment programs).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of International Monetary Fund.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: Established in 1944 at the **Bretton Woods Conference** along with the World Bank, commencing operations in December 1945 with headquarters in Washington, D.C.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: Operates primarily through **Quotas** (capital subscriptions) which determine a member country's voting power, financial contribution, and maximum borrowing limit.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: Acts as the lender of last resort for countries facing acute **Balance of Payments (BoP)** crises, conditioned upon implementing economic reform programs (Structural Adjustment Programs).
• **Key Metric / Factor**: **Special Drawing Rights (SDR)** serve as the IMF's unit of account and a potential claim against the freely usable currencies of IMF members.

Reviewed every 5 years by the IMF Executive Board based on export volume and financial use.
Frequent Prelims questions on currency composition and weightage hierarchy.
Stand-By Arrangements (SBA), Extended Fund Facility (EFF), Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust (PRGT).
Tailored to short-term liquidity needs versus long-term structural structural reforms.
Distinguishing short-term vs structural credit tranches for developing economies.
Board of Governors (highest policy-making body, one per country) and Executive Board (24 Directors managing daily business).
Weighted voting system based on financial quotas; US and EU hold significant veto power blocks.
Mains debates on democratic deficit and governance reforms in Bretton Woods institutions.

items.definition: Each member country is assigned a quota based on its relative position in the world economy. Quotas determine financial contributions, voting power, and access to IMF financing.
An international reserve asset created by the IMF in 1969 to supplement its member countries' official reserves. It is not a currency but a basket of major currencies.
Bilateral discussions between IMF staff and member country authorities held usually every year, assessing economic health and providing policy advice to prevent financial instability.
World Economic Outlook (WEO), Global Financial Stability Report (GFSR), and Fiscal Monitor published biannually ahead of IMF/World Bank meetings.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Region / Zone Details**: 190 member states with regional surveillance offices across Washington D.C., Tokyo, Paris, Geneva, Vienna, and Singapore.
• **Driving Advantages**: Global macroeconomic surveillance, localized technical assistance centers (e.g., CARTAC in the Caribbean, AFRITAC in Africa) for capacity building.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Quota formula delays, underrepresentation of emerging markets (like India and China), and strict austerity conditions triggering social unrest.
• **Policy Interventions**: Ongoing quota reviews, integration of climate change risks into macroeconomic surveillance, and debt relief initiatives for low-income countries (HIPC/MDRI).

items.title: Mnemonic for SDR Basket Currencies
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "BIG U&E" or "MY USD CUP" (Modified: **U**S Dollar, **E**uro, **C**hinese Yuan/Renminbi, **J**apanese Yen, **B**ritish Pound -> **U-E-R-Y-B**).
• **Decoded Meaning**: US Dollar, Euro, Renminbi, Yen, Pound.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly identifies inclusion or exclusion of currencies like the Indian Rupee or Swiss Franc (which are NOT in the SDR basket).

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: IMF = Lender of last resort for **Balance of Payments (BoP)**; World Bank = Long-term lender for **Development and Infrastructure projects**.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that 'SDR is a currency of the IMF' or 'Indian Rupee is part of the SDR basket'. Both are FALSE. SDR is an international reserve asset, and the Rupee is not part of the SDR basket.

Mains Value Addition: Emphasize the need for 'Quota Reforms' to reflect contemporary economic weight (such as purchasing power parity adjustments) to enhance the legitimacy and effectiveness of global economic governance.

keyTakeaways: The IMF was formed at Bretton Woods to ensure global financial stability and manage Balance of Payments crises.
Voting power is determined by financial quotas, making quota reform a persistent geopolitical debate.
SDR is an artificial basket of five major currencies used as the IMF's unit of account, excluding the Indian Rupee.
